neighbours.label: a running sum reaching its total: ' to' in 'add(s) up to' and the verb ' totals' before an amount; weaker on line ends of accumulating statements in a code loop
fire: She reads twenty pages a night, which adds up to about two books a month.
Three coffees a day adds up to more than a thousand cups a year.
The small leaks around the house add up to hundreds of litres each week.
He cycles nine miles each way, which adds up to ninety miles a week.
A few cents on every order adds up to millions over a decade.
The club charges ten euros a session, which totals about five hundred euros a year.
Two minutes of delay per train totals nearly an hour by evening.
Those ten-minute breaks add up to almost a full working day each month.
quiet: She reads twenty pages a night and finishes about two books a month.
Three coffees a day is more than a doctor would recommend.
The small leaks around the house amount to a serious nuisance each winter.
He cycles nine miles each way, from the village to the factory.
A few cents on every order goes to a local charity.
The club charges ten euros a session and closes in August.
The repair bill came to nearly ninety pounds in the end.
The price went up to almost a full dollar per litre.

notes: Card: top example is 'adds up to'; the rest are line ends after append/accumulate statements in Python loops. Probes: 'adds up to' 0.91, 'add up to' 0.53, 'which totals' 0.69, loop bodies 0.28-0.37, 'amount to' 0.01, 'came to' 0.01, 'works out to' 0.04, 'from..to' 0.01. Tested on the prose form only.
